memory_candidates: `classical` (invoked before Finset.induction/Function.update in the same tactic block scope) DOES resolve DecidableEq (Label Atom) for a generic Atom parameter via Classical.propDecidable-backed instance resolution -- this corrects the Phase 4.1 dispatch's dead_ends note, which claimed Function.update fails without a directly-supplied DecidableEq instance. It works fine as long as `classical` precedes the relevant tactic call in the same proof scope.

cs5FCIncest's raised-witness conjuncts (hfour/hsymbox/hincest) have no 'raise one endpoint, keep the other exact' variant, so raising one endpoint of an r-edge always forces the other to move too (to some >=-successor). This makes any 'lift the interpretation at one label' construction over a graph inherently a CASCADE over that label's raw-connected component, not a local, single-hop operation -- true generality requires an acyclicity/rank invariant on the graph, verified necessary via a concrete 3-cycle counterexample (unique-parent-per-target alone is insufficient).
